name: Japanese · Phrases · Health and pharmacy
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.note: Telling family or friends. Particle dropped as in speech.
Telling a doctor, nurse or teacher.

entries.term: ちょっと熱っぽいんです。
entries.reading: ちょっとねつっぽいんです
entries.note: To a doctor or when calling in. 〜っぽい = feels like.
Everyday complaint at home or with friends.
Often the first sign of a cold or flu.

entries.back: I think I'm going to throw up.
entries.note: Urgent warning to whoever's with you.
Telling a doctor or someone helping you.

entries.term: 咳がなかなか治らないんだ。
entries.reading: せきがなかなかなおらないんだ
entries.note: Telling a friend about a lingering cough.
Listing symptoms at a clinic or pharmacy.
Telling friends or family.
Doctor or nurse asking. Point and say ここです.

entries.term: 症状はいつからですか？
entries.reading: しょうじょうはいつからですか
entries.note: Doctor's standard question. Answer e.g. 昨日からです.

entries.term: 保険証はお持ちですか？
entries.reading: ほけんしょうはおもちですか
entries.back: Do you have your insurance card?
entries.note: Asked at clinic reception every visit.
Telling reception you're a new patient.

entries.term: アレルギーは特にありません。
entries.reading: アレルギーはとくにありません
entries.back: No allergies that I know of.
entries.note: Answering the doctor or the intake form.

entries.reading: ずつうやくはありますか
entries.back: Do you have anything for headaches?
entries.note: Asking at a drugstore counter.

entries.term: 処方箋をお預かりします。
entries.reading: しょほうせんをおあずかりします
entries.note: Pharmacy staff as you hand over the prescription.

entries.term: 一日三回、食後に飲んでください。
entries.reading: いちにちさんかいしょくごにのんでください
entries.back: Take it three times a day after meals.
entries.note: Pharmacist explaining the dosage.
Said to anyone who's ill, and by clinic staff as you leave.
Checking on a sick friend or family member.

entries.reading: たいちょうがわるいの
entries.note: When someone looks pale or off.

entries.term: 病院行った方がいいよ。
entries.reading: びょういんいったほうがいいよ
entries.note: Urging a friend. 病院 covers clinics too.

entries.back: Why don't you take your temperature?
entries.note: Suggesting it to someone who feels hot or tired.
Parent or partner checking.

entries.reading: くすりをのみわすれた
entries.back: I forgot to take my medicine.
entries.note: Realizing it at home. 飲む is used for pills too.

entries.term: 薬のおかげで楽になったよ。
entries.reading: くすりのおかげでらくになったよ
entries.note: Reporting back to someone who asked how you are.
Caring line to someone sick or overworked.
Very common complaint; 腰 is the lower back.

entries.reading: かふんしょうつらいよね
entries.back: Hay fever is the worst, isn't it?
entries.note: Spring small talk — huge numbers of people in Japan have it.

entries.term: 風邪治ってよかったね。
entries.reading: かぜなおってよかったね
entries.note: Said to a friend who's recovered.
Explaining why you're away or can't come.
